body: Big scientific puzzles can start with things you can actually observe. Darwin says studying domesticated plants and animals gave him the “best and safest clue” to how species vary.
evidenceQuote: I have invariably found that our knowledge, imperfect though it be, of variation under domestication, afforded the best and safest clue.

body: A boy got tired of opening and closing a steam-engine valve, so he rigged it to work by itself and went back to playing. Smith says one of that machine’s biggest improvements started with a kid trying to save his own effort.
evidenceQuote: One of the greatest improvements that has been made upon this machine, since it was first invented, was in this manner the discovery of a boy who wanted to save his own labour.

body: A 2,000-year-old call-out for “I’ll do it tomorrow.” Marcus Aurelius reminds himself how many times he has already put things off.
evidenceQuote: Remember how long thou hast already put off these things, and how often a certain day and hour as it were, having been set unto thee by the gods, thou hast neglected it.
